findings.explanation: The node pool sets both node_count and an autoscaling block. Once the cluster autoscaler resizes the pool in response to load, node_count in state drifts from var.node_pool["node_count"]. Without lifecycle.ignore_changes = [node_count], a subsequent terraform apply plans to resize the pool back to the configured value, undoing the autoscaler's decision and potentially evicting workloads under load.
findings.remediation: Add a lifecycle block ignoring node_count so Terraform stops fighting the autoscaler.
findings.title: Node pool has no lifecycle.ignore_changes on node_count while autoscaling is enabled

findings.explanation: variables.tf's node_pool default map includes auto_repair and auto_upgrade keys (README's generated table documents them as inputs), but the management block hardcoded both to true, ignoring any value a caller supplies. Callers reasonably believe these are configurable when they are not.
findings.remediation: Wire management.auto_repair / management.auto_upgrade from var.node_pool via lookup(), defaulting to true so existing callers are unaffected.
findings.title: node_pool variable exposes auto_repair/auto_upgrade keys that the resource silently ignores
